questions.question: If sin θ = \(\frac{11}{12}\) , then what will be the value of (tan θ + sec θ) ?
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ = \(\frac{11}{12}\), then what will be the value of (tan θ + sec θ) ?
questions.solution:
sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 (11/12)2 + cos2θ = 1 121/144 + cos2θ = 1 cos2θ =

23/144 cos θ = √(23/144) = √23/12

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ tan θ = (11/12) / (√23/12) = 11 / √23 sec θ = 1 / cos θ

sec θ = 12 / √23

tan θ + sec θ = (11 / √23) + (12 / √23) tan θ + sec θ = (11 + 12) / √23 tan θ

+ sec θ = 23 / √23 = √23

questions.question: Evaluate (9 sin θ + 2 cos θ) / (9 sin θ − 2 cos θ), if 3 tan θ = 4.
questions.questionHtml: Evaluate (9 sin θ + 2 cos θ) / (9 sin θ − 2 cos θ), if 3 tan θ = 4.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given 3 tan θ = 4 ⇒ tan θ = 4/3.

Divide the numerator and denominator by cos θ to convert the expression into tan θ.

Expression = (9 tan θ + 2) / (9 tan θ − 2)

Substitute tan θ = 4/3 ⇒ (9 × 4/3 + 2) / (9 × 4/3 − 2) = (12 + 2) / (12 − 2) = 14 / 10 = 7/5.

∴ The correct answer is 7/5.

Alternate Method

Given: 3 tan θ = 4

Formula Used: tan θ = Perpendicular / Base; sin θ = P/H; cos θ = B/H

⇒ tan θ = 4/3

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 4, Base (B) = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(P2 + B2) = √(42 + 32) = √25 = 5

⇒ sin θ = 4/5 and cos θ = 3/5

⇒ (9 × 4/5 + 2 × 3/5) / (9 × 4/5 − 2 × 3/5)

⇒ (36/5 + 6/5) / (36/5 − 6/5) = (42/5) / (30/5)

⇒ 42 / 30 = 7/5

∴ The correct answer is 7/5.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

Fundamental ratios are sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H, and tan θ = P/B.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers (a, b, c) such that a2 + b2 = c2. Common triplets include (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13).

Ratio Transformation

An expression involving sin θ and cos θ of the same degree can be simplified by dividing by cos θ or sin θ to convert it into tan θ or cot θ.

questions.question: if cot θ = \(\frac{15}{8}\) , θ is an acute angle, then find the value of \(\rm \frac{(1-cos\theta)(2+2cos\theta)}{(2-2sin\theta)(1+sin\theta)}\) .
questions.questionHtml: if cot θ = \(\frac{15}{8}\), θ is an acute angle, then find the value of \(\rm \frac{(1-cos\theta)(2+2cos\theta)}{(2-2sin\theta)(1+sin\theta)}\).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplify the expression using the identity (1 − cos2 θ) = sin2 θ and (1 − sin2 θ) = cos2 θ.

Expression = [2(1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] ÷ [2(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] = (1 − cos2 θ) ÷ (1 − sin2 θ).

This simplifies directly to sin2 θ ÷ cos2 θ = tan2 θ.

Since cot θ = 15/8, then tan θ = 8/15.

Result = (8/15)2 = 64/225.

∴ The correct answer is 64/225.

Alternate Method

Given: cot θ = 15/8, where θ is an acute angle.

In a right-angled triangle, cot θ = Base / Perpendicular.

Using Pythagoras Theorem: H2 = P2 + B2 ⇒ H2 = 82 + 152 = 64 + 225 = 289 ⇒ H = 17.

Formula Used: (a − b)(a + b) = a2 − b2

Expression = ((1 − cos θ)(2 + 2 cos θ)) / ((2 − 2 sin θ)(1 + sin θ))

⇒ [2 × (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] / [2 × (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ (1 − cos2 θ) / (1 − sin2 θ)

By trigonometric identities: 1 − cos2 θ = sin2 θ and 1 − sin2 θ = cos2 θ

⇒ sin2 θ / cos2 θ = tan2 θ

⇒ (1 / cot θ)2

⇒ (1 / (15/8))2 = (8/15)2

⇒ 64 / 225

∴ The correct answer is 64/225.

Additional Information

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1 | 2. 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ | 3. 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Reciprocal Relations

tan θ = 1 / cot θ, sec θ = 1 / cos θ, and cosec θ = 1 / sin θ.

Pythagorean Triplet

For a right-angled triangle with sides (8, 15, 17), the square of the largest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (172 = 82 + 152).

questions.question: If sin x – cos x = 0, 0° < x < 90° then the value of (sec x + cosec x) 2 is:
questions.questionHtml: If sin x – cos x = 0, 0° < x < 90° then the value of (sec x + cosec x)<sup>2</sup> is:
questions.solution:
Given

sin x – cos x = 0

Calculation

sin x – cos x = 0

⇒ sinx = cosx

⇒ sinx = sin(90° - x)

⇒ x = 90° - x

⇒ 2x = 90°

⇒ x = 45°

Now,

(sec x + cosec x)2 

= (sec 45° + cosec 45°)2

= (√2 + √2)2

= (2√2)2

= 8

\(\frac{9 \sin x - \frac{42}{5}\cos x}{15 \sin x + 21 \cos x}\)

questions.question: If \(\frac{{\sin A + \cos A}}{{\cos A}} = \frac{{17}}{{12}},\) then the value of \(\frac{{1 - \cos A}}{{\sin A}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{{\sin A + \cos A}}{{\cos A}} = \frac{{17}}{{12}},\) then the value of \(\frac{{1 - \cos A}}{{\sin A}}\) is:
questions.solution:
sinA + cosA/cosA = 17/12

⇒ 12 sin A + 12 cos A = 17 cos A

⇒ 12 sin A = 5 cos A

⇒ sin A/cos A = 5/12

⇒ tanA = 5/12

⇒ tanA = P/B = 5/12

Perpendicular = P, Base = B and Hypotenuse = H

P = 5 and B = 12

H2 = P2 + B2

⇒ H2 = 122 + 52

⇒ H2 = 144 + 25

⇒ H2 = 169

⇒ H = √169

⇒ H = 13

sin A = P/H = 5/13

cos A = B/H = 12/13

Now,

⇒ (1 - cos A)/sinA

⇒ (1 - 12/13)/5/13

⇒ (1/13)/(5/13)

⇒ 1/5

questions.question: If cosec θ = \(\frac{41}{9}\) and θ is an acute angle, then the value of 5 tan θ will be:
questions.questionHtml: If cosec θ = \(\frac{41}{9}\) and θ is an acute angle, then the value of 5 tan θ will be:
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodExam approach - 

41, 9 and 40 make a triplet.

Given that cosecθ = 41/9. It means Hypotenuse = 41 and Perpendicular = 9. Therefore, base = 40

tanθ = Perpendicular/Base

⇒ tan θ = 9/40

⇒ 5tan θ = 5 × (9/40) = 9/8

∴ The required value is 9/8.

Traditional method:

Given:

cosec θ = \(\frac{41}{9}\) 

Formula:

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

Calculation:

sin θ = 9/41

cos θ = √(1 - (9/41)2) = 40/41

tan θ = (sinθ)/(cosθ) = (9/41) × (41/40) = 9/40

∴ 5 tanθ = 5 × 9/40 = 9/8

questions.question: If tanθ = 4/3, then the value of \(\frac{9\sin θ+12\cos θ}{27\cos θ-20\sin θ}\) will be equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If tanθ = 4/3, then the value of \(\frac{9\sin θ+12\cos θ}{27\cos θ-20\sin θ}\) will be equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

tanθ = 4/3

Concept used:

tanθ = p/b, sinθ = p/h, cosθ = b/h

h2 = p2 + b2

(where p = Perpendicular, b = Base, h = Hypotenuse)

Calculation:

tanθ = 4/3, So, p = 4 and b = 3

Now, h2 = 42 + 32 = 16 + 9 = 25

⇒ h2 = 25

⇒ h = 5

Now, sinθ = 4/5, cosθ = 3/5

So, (9sinθ + 12cosθ)/(27cosθ – 20sinθ) = (9 × 4/5 + 12 × 3/5)/(27 × 3/5 - 20 × 4/5)

= (36/5 + 36/5)/(81/5 - 80/5)

= (72/5)/(1/5)

= 72

∴ The required value is 72

Shortcut Trick

\(\frac{9\sin θ+12\cos θ}{27\cos θ-20\sin θ}\)

Taking cosθ as common from both numerator and denominator, we can write:

\(\frac{cosθ~ (9\tan θ+12)}{cosθ~ (27-20~tanθ)}=\frac{ 9\tan θ+12}{ 27-20~tanθ}\)

Putting tanθ = 4/3, we get the required answer of 72.

questions.questionHtml: If sin (a + b) = 1 and cos (a - b) = \(\frac{1}{2} \), then find a.

cos(A – B) = 1/2 ⇒ cos(A – B) = cos60° ⇒ A – B = 60° .....(2)

Adding equation (1) and (2), we get

⇒ 2A = 150° ⇒ A = 75°

questions.question: The value of sin 35° cos 55° + cos 35° sin 55° is:

sin 35° cos 55° + cos 35° sin 55°

questions.question: Find the value of \(\dfrac{\tan 60^\circ - \tan 15^\circ}{1 + \tan 60^\circ \tan 15^\circ}\)
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of \(\dfrac{\tan 60^\circ - \tan 15^\circ}{1 + \tan 60^\circ \tan 15^\circ}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\dfrac{\tan 60^\circ - \tan 15^\circ}{1 + \tan 60^\circ \tan 15^\circ}\)

Formula:

tan (A - B) = (tan A - tan B)/(1 + tan A tan B)

tan 45° = 1

Calculation:

(tan 60° - tan 15°)/(1 + tan 60° tan 15°)

⇒ tan (60° - 15°)

⇒ tan 45°

⇒ 1

questions.question: If \(sin A=\frac{1}{2}\) , A is an acute angle, then find the value of \(\frac{tan A-cot A}{\sqrt 3(1+cosecA)}\) .
questions.questionHtml: If \(sin A=\frac{1}{2}\), A is an acute angle, then find the value of \(\frac{tan A-cot A}{\sqrt 3(1+cosecA)}\).
questions.solution:
Given:

Sin A = 1/2

Formula used:

Sin 30° = 1/2

tan 30° = 1/√3

Cot 30° = √3

Cosec 30° = 2

Calculation:

Sin A = 1/2

⇒ A = 30° 

Now put the value of A in given equation we get,

\(\frac{tan A-cot A}{√ 3(1+cosecA)}\)

⇒ tan 30° – cot 30°/√3(1 + cosec 30°)

⇒ (1/√3 – √3)/√3(1 + 2)

⇒ [(1 – 3)/√3]/3√3

⇒ (-2/√3)/3√3

⇒ -2/9

∴ Required value is \(-\frac{2}{9}\)

questions.question: If 5cosθ – 12sinθ = 0, then value of \(\frac{{2sin\theta \; + \;cos\theta }}{{cos\theta \; - \;sin\theta }}\;\) is∶
questions.questionHtml: If 5cosθ – 12sinθ = 0, then value of \(\frac{{2sin\theta \; + \;cos\theta }}{{cos\theta \; - \;sin\theta }}\;\)is∶
questions.solution:
We know that, sinθ/cosθ = tanθ

Given∶ 5cosθ – 12sinθ = 0

⇒ 5cosθ = 12sinθ

⇒ sinθ/cosθ = 5/12

⇒ tanθ = 5/12 -     ---1

\(\frac{{2sin\theta \; + \;cos\theta }}{{cos\theta \; - \;sin\theta }}\; = \;\frac{{cos\theta \left( {\frac{{2sin\theta \;}}{{cos\theta }}\; + \;1} \right)}}{{cos\theta \left( {1\; - \;\frac{{sin\theta \;}}{{cos\theta }}\;} \right)}}\; = \;\frac{{\left( {2tan\theta \; + \;1} \right)}}{{\left( {1\; - tan\theta \;} \right)}}\)

Put the value of tanθ from equation 1 into above expression,

\( \Rightarrow \frac{{\left( {2tan\theta \; + \;1} \right)}}{{\left( {1\; - tan\theta \;} \right)}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{2\; \times \;5\;}}{{12}}\; + \;1} \right)}}{{\left( {1\; - \;\frac{{5\;}}{{12}}\;} \right)}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{10\;}}{{12}}\; + \;1} \right)}}{{\left( {1\; - \;\frac{{5\;}}{{12}}\;} \right)}} = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{22\;}}{{12}}} \right)}}{{\left( {\frac{{7\;}}{{12}}\;} \right)}} = \frac{{22}}{7} = 3\frac{1}{7}\)

questions.question: If 5 sin θ = 4, then the value of \(\frac{{sec\theta + 4\cot \theta }}{{4tan\theta - 5cos\theta }}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 5 sin θ = 4, then the value of \(\frac{{sec\theta + 4\cot \theta }}{{4tan\theta - 5cos\theta }}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

5 sin θ = 4

∴  sin θ = 4/5

We have to calculate the value of \(\frac{{sec\theta + 4\cot \theta }}{{4tan\theta - 5cos\theta }}\)

Calculation:

Perpendicular = P, Hypotenuse = H and Base = B.

sin θ = P/H = 4/5

P = 4 and H = 5

As we know,

H2 = P2 + B2

⇒ 52 = 42 + B2

⇒ B2 = 25 – 16 = 9

⇒ B = √9 = 3

⇒ cos θ = B/H = 3/5

⇒ sec θ = 1/cos θ = 5/3

tan θ = P/B = 4/3

cot θ = 1/tan θ = 3/4

Now,

\(\frac{{sec\theta + 4\cot \theta }}{{4tan\theta - 5cos\theta }}\)

\( \Rightarrow \frac{{\frac{5}{3} + 4 \times \frac{3}{4}}}{{4 \times \frac{4}{3} - 5 \times \frac{3}{5}}}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{{\frac{5}{3} + 3}}{{\frac{{16}}{3} - 3}}\)

\( \Rightarrow \frac{{\frac{{14}}{3}}}{{\frac{7}{3}}}\)

⇒ 2

So, the value is 2.

questions.question: If sin θ + cosec θ = 2, then the value of sin 2 θ + cosec 2 θ is:
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ + cosec θ = 2, then the value of sin<sup>2 </sup>θ + cosec<sup>2</sup> θ is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sinθ + cosecθ = 2

Formula Used:

cosecθ = 1/sinθ

Calculation:

Let sinθ = x

⇒ sinθ + cosecθ = x + 1/x = 2

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 22

⇒ x2 + 2 + 1/x2 = 4

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 2

∴ sin2θ + cosec2θ = 2

questions.question: 2 cos θ + sec θ - 2√2 = 0, where θ is an acute angle. Find the value of θ.
questions.questionHtml: 2 cos θ + sec θ - 2√2 = 0, where θ is an acute angle. Find the value of θ.
questions.solution:
Calculation:

2 cos θ + sec θ - 2√2 = 0

⇒ 2 cos θ + 1/ cos θ - 2√2 = 0

⇒ 2 cos2 θ + 1 - 2√2 cos θ = 0

⇒ 2 cos2 θ - 2√2 cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2 cos2 θ - √2 cos θ - √2 cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ √2 cos θ (√2 cos θ - 1) - 1(√2 cos θ - 1) = 0

⇒ (√2 cos θ - 1)2 = 0

⇒ √2 cos θ - 1 = 0

⇒ √2 cos θ = 1 

⇒ cos θ = 1/√2 

∴ cos 45° = 1/√2 

⇒ θ = 45°

Alternate Method By value putting:

θ = 45° 

2 cos θ + sec θ - 2√2 = 0 

⇒ 2 × 1/√2  + √2  - 2√2 = 0 

⇒ 2√2 - 2√2 = 0

At values θ = 30° , 60° and 15°, the above condition is not fulfilled. Hence, 45° is the correct value of θ.
